verification.fact_verification_explanation: Supported: the account was reported to the credit bureaus as '60 days past due' on 2026-04-20, so the customer's allegation that this status appears on their credit report is consistent with the records. Contradicted: the claim that no payment was ever missed and every payment was on time. The scheduled $140.00 installments on 2026-03-18 and 2026-04-18 were both 'not received'. The account was brought current by a $280.00 payment on 2026-05-18 covering 2 installments, and the 2026-06-18 installment was received. Payments on 2026-01-18 and 2026-02-18 were on time. Reviewer note: on 2026-04-20 the oldest unpaid installment (2026-03-18) was only about 33 days past due, so a '60 days past due' status looks overstated on these dates. The cause is not explained in the records, so the delinquency level reported should be checked before any response states it was accurate. Also, no record shows whether the bureau tradeline was updated after the 2026-05-18 catch-up payment. Transaction history only covers 2026-01 to 2026-06, so the customer's 18-month on-time claim cannot be checked for earlier months. This does not change the finding on the March and April missed installments.
verification.risk_rationale: The claim is partially_true (the missed March and April payments contradict the customer, but the 60-day reporting level may be overstated), and it involves credit-reporting accuracy; there is no attorney/regulator reference, hardship, vulnerability, or UDAAP-pattern language, so it does not reach High.

policy.text:
# Policy: Credit Reporting Disputes (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

**Applies to:** Any complaint alleging inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information reported to a consumer reporting agency (credit bureau).

## Requirements
- As a furnisher of information, we must investigate a dispute (received either directly from the consumer or relayed by a credit bureau) within **30 days**, extendable to **45 days** if the consumer provides additional information during the 30-day window.
- We must review all relevant information provided by the consumer, correct any inaccuracy found, and report the results of the investigation back to the consumer and, if applicable, to the credit bureau.
- If an item is found to be inaccurate or unverifiable, it must be corrected or deleted from our reporting **promptly**.
- We may not resume reporting an item we previously deleted unless we can certify the information is accurate and complete.
- A consumer may request a statement of the dispute to be included in their credit file if the dispute is not resolved to their satisfaction.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May confirm whether our internal records match or contradict what is reported (e.g., payment history, account status).
- May state the applicable 30/45-day investigation timeline.
- May NOT promise a specific bureau will update within a specific number of days — we control our own furnishing, not the bureau's processing timeline.

## Escalation trigger
A **third or subsequent dispute on the same item**, or any complaint stating an investigation was closed with no explanation of what was actually checked, should be escalated — repeated unresolved disputes carry elevated regulatory risk.

## Remedy authority
Front-line staff may initiate a correction to our own furnished data (status, balance, payment history) when the internal transaction record clearly supports the correction. Removing an account entirely, or correcting identity-mismatch issues, requires supervisor or fraud-team review.

*Source: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq. Generic, illustrative summary for internal training/demo purposes, not legal advice.*

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us because your credit report shows this account as 60 days past due, and you believe every payment over the past 18 months was made on time. We reviewed your account's payment records. Here is what we found on each point.

Credit report status: Our records show the account was reported to the credit bureaus as "60 days past due" on April 20, 2026. So the status you saw matches what we reported. On that date, though, the oldest unpaid installment (due March 18, 2026) was about 33 days past due. We are reviewing whether the 60-day status was reported correctly, and we have not concluded that it was accurate.

Payment history: Our records show the $140.00 installments due March 18 and April 18, 2026 as not received. The January 18 and February 18 payments were received on time. A $280.00 payment on May 18, 2026 covered the two missed installments, and the June 18 installment was received.

18 months of on-time payments: The payment history available to us covers January through June 2026, so we cannot confirm or dispute your on-time record for earlier months. For January through June 2026, our records do not show every payment as on time, for the reasons above.

Outcome: We are investigating the reported status as a credit reporting dispute. We will complete the investigation within 30 days, or up to 45 days if you send us additional information during that time. If we find that what we reported was inaccurate, we will correct it and tell you the results. We cannot say when any credit bureau will update its records, because the bureaus control their own processing.

Next steps: If you have bank statements showing payments on March 18 or April 18, 2026, or statements for earlier months, please reply with copies so we can include them in the review. If the dispute is not resolved to your satisfaction, you may ask that a statement of the dispute be added to your credit file. You are also free to contact any other agency or advisor about this matter.

Case reference: 23623033
